pr_body:
Today a force-merge will write out the newly-merged segments and then
flush them, but it does not automatically release the segments from
before the merge. This will retain extra data on disk until the next
refresh, which could be a long time away if the user has disabled
periodic refreshes or is not searching the index frequently.

With this commit we change the behaviour always to refresh after a
force-merge.

Closes #74649

review_comment: In the case of anyone force merging against an index that still receives writes, I think this risks writing a new segment for the refresh. I did not look whether it is possible, but it would be ideal if we could somehow refresh to the latest available segment?

I'm not sure I follow. Do you mean to refresh to the segments we just flushed, even if there are newer ones on disk? We don't necessarily flush exactly the result of the force-merge either, we're free to do more merges before flushing.

In principle we're fairly free to write out new segments and/or refresh whenever we decide it's appropriate. For instance we effectively refresh when moving a shard onto a different node, which may happen at any time.

Technically the Lucene API does let us reopen the underlying `DirectoryReader` to a specific index commit, but that's not something we ever do in Elasticsearch at the moment and I think it'd be excessively hard to do so here. We'd need to protect against things like undoing the effects of a concurrent refresh, for example.

It was only to avoid writing out new segments, for instance if the index has refresh completely disabled.

But I thought the complexity would be somewhat like you described and I am good with how it is. Thanks for entertaining me!

🕺

I see. Even if refresh is completely disabled we still write new segments to disk for lots of other reasons (e.g. if the indexing buffer or the translog gets too full). We just don't reopen the reader on the new segments as much, but we're not forbidden from doing so either.
